skill.name: authentication-setup
skill.description: Create authentication and authorization implementations for web applications, including passwords, JWT tokens, OAuth, sessions, RBAC, and security controls.
skill.summary: Guides secure authentication design, implementation, and review for application backends.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, safe examples, reference links, and placeholder environment variables. I found no prompt injection, hidden execution, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent. One semantic issue remains: the generated refresh-token pattern stores reusable bearer tokens and omits rotation.

remediation.issue: Refresh tokens are stored as raw reusable bearer tokens in examples.
remediation.suggestion: Hash refresh tokens before storage, store only a lookup fingerprint, rotate tokens on each refresh, and revoke old tokens on logout.

remediation.issue: Example handlers return raw server error messages in API responses.
remediation.suggestion: Return generic client errors and log detailed exception data only on the server side.

remediation.issue: Rate limiting is required in prose but not shown in endpoint examples.
remediation.suggestion: Add concrete rate limiting guidance for registration, login, password reset, and refresh endpoints.

semantic_findings.title: Refresh Token Handling Stores Reusable Bearer Tokens
semantic_findings.description: The examples store raw refresh tokens in the database and look them up by the same token value. A database leak would expose reusable bearer tokens until expiry, and the refresh flow does not rotate tokens on use.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code examples directly persist token: refreshToken and query where token equals the presented refresh token. This is a common production weakness even though the skill is instructional.

content.value_statement: Authentication is hard to implement without weak passwords, unsafe tokens, or missing authorization. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through secure auth setup.
actual_capabilities: Designs user, refresh token, and OAuth provider data models for common databases.
Provides password hashing and verification patterns using bcrypt or argon2.
Generates JWT access and refresh token flows with environment-based secrets.
Creates authentication middleware and role-based authorization checks for APIs.
Outlines registration, login, refresh, current-user, and protected-route workflows.
Lists security constraints for HTTPS, CORS, input validation, MFA, and audit logging.
limitations: Examples focus mainly on Express.js and TypeScript, so other frameworks need adaptation.
The skill gives implementation guidance, not a complete audited production auth package.
OAuth provider details are high level and require provider-specific setup steps.
Generated code still needs tests, threat modeling, and review by security owners.

use_cases.title: Add Login to a New API
use_cases.description: Plan user registration, password hashing, JWT issuance, refresh tokens, and protected API routes for a new backend.

use_cases.title: Introduce Role-Based Access Control
use_cases.description: Add middleware and route policies that separate administrator actions from standard user access.

use_cases.title: Review an Authentication Migration
use_cases.description: Check a migration to JWT, sessions, or OAuth for token lifetime, secret handling, CORS, MFA, and audit logging gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic JWT Auth
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new backend.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic JWT login system for [framework] with [database]. Include password hashing, registration, login, and protected route middleware.

prompt_templates.title: Design Session Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Design authentication for [app] using sessions instead of JWT. Include storage, cookie settings, CSRF protection, and logout behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Add OAuth Providers
prompt_templates.prompt: Add OAuth login with [providers] to an existing [framework] app. Map provider accounts, handle account linking, and document environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Auth
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this authentication design for production risks. Check token lifetime, refresh token rotation, RBAC, MFA, rate limiting, CORS, and audit logging.

output_examples.input: Add JWT authentication to an Express API with PostgreSQL and refresh tokens.
output: A user and refresh-token data model with indexes for email and token lookup.
Password hashing and verification guidance using bcrypt with strong salt settings.
Registration, login, refresh, and current-user route behavior described in order.
Middleware guidance for bearer token validation and role checks.

output_examples.input: Review my planned OAuth and RBAC design before implementation.
output: A checklist covering provider account linking, environment variables, scopes, and callback handling.
RBAC route rules for administrator-only actions and standard user actions.
Security notes for MFA, rate limiting, audit logging, and CORS origin restrictions.

output_examples.input: Create a production readiness checklist for an existing login system.
output: Items for password storage, token expiration, refresh token revocation, and HTTPS enforcement.
Operational checks for secret rotation, audit logs, database indexes, and failed-login monitoring.
Testing guidance for invalid tokens, expired sessions, unauthorized roles, and duplicate accounts.

best_practices: Use the skill with a clear framework, database, token strategy, and security requirements.
Ask for a threat-focused review after generating authentication code or architecture.
Replace placeholders with secret-manager values and test every login and authorization path.
anti_patterns: Do not paste production secrets, real tokens, or customer credentials into prompts.
Do not ship generated authentication code without tests and manual security review.
Do not hardcode JWT secrets, OAuth secrets, database URLs, or allowed CORS origins.

faq.question: Can this skill build a complete login system?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation and produce code patterns, but the result still needs testing and security review.

faq.question: Which authentication methods does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers JWT, session-based login, OAuth 2.0, refresh tokens, RBAC, and optional MFA planning.

faq.question: Does it support non-Node frameworks?
faq.answer: Yes, but the strongest examples are for Express.js and TypeScript. Other stacks need framework-specific adaptation.

faq.question: Can I include real secrets in the prompt?
faq.answer: No. Use placeholders and configure real secrets through your deployment environment or secret manager.

faq.question: Does it replace a security audit?
faq.answer: No. It helps design and review authentication, but production systems need independent security validation.

faq.question: Can it review existing authentication code?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide relevant files and ask it to check password storage, token handling, RBAC, CORS, and logging.
